families.absolute-scale-clean-negative-r.formal: The other half of the weight problem, why $\mathrm{Im}\,w_{e} \sim 10^{38}$ at all (Fact \claimref{families.imported-dictionary-exact-join}), resists every structural attack attempted: expressing the imaginary weights as powers of $N$ finds no clean exponent for the electron or the weak scale, and the one suggestive scaling (a hadronic weight $\mathrm{Im}\,w_{h} \sim N^{2/3}$ with $N = M_{P}/H$ of Fact \claimref{standard-model.trichotomy-what-kind-number}, equivalently $m_{h} \sim (M_{P}^{2}H)^{1/3} \approx 5 \times 10^{7}$ eV on the inputs of Proposition \claimref{families.alignment-computed-thirteenth-refutation-democracy-one}(1), the pion-scale coincidence) reduces to the Zel'dovich-Weinberg coincidence, in the literature since 1967 \cite{Zeldovich1967, Weinberg1972}, and therefore fails the series' prior-art condition. Counting the tower's hyperbolic pairs, mode-count ratios, and fine-structure powers all fail their own refutation conditions. The absolute hierarchy remains as the fifth and thirteenth refutations left it: one unexplained number, restated, with a map of the routes that do not work.
families.absolute-scale-clean-negative-r.technical:
The observation concerns the second half of the weight problem: why the imaginary part of the electron's induced weight is of order $10^{38}$ at all, given that a heavy composite has weight $w = -\tfrac32 \pm I_4\nu$ with $\nu \approx m/H$ (numbers are read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_4\}$). Writing the imaginary weights as powers of $N = M_{P}/H$ gives no clean exponent for the electron or the weak scale. The one suggestive scaling, a hadronic weight $\mathrm{Im}\,w_{h} \sim N^{2/3}$, equivalently $m_{h} \sim (M_{P}^{2}H)^{1/3} \approx 5 \times 10^{7}$ eV, is the Zel'dovich-Weinberg coincidence, in the literature since 1967, and so fails the series' prior-art condition.

Counting the tower's hyperbolic pairs, mode-count ratios and powers of the fine-structure constant each fail their own refutation conditions. The absolute hierarchy remains one unexplained number, restated, together with a map of the routes that do not work.
families.absolute-scale-clean-negative-r.lay: In this framework a particle's mass is coded by a number, its weight, measured against the tiny scale set by the cosmological constant. For ordinary particles that number is enormous, around $10^{38}$ for the electron, and nothing in the framework yet explains why. Several natural attempts were tried and all fail, one of them because it only rediscovers a coincidence first noticed in 1967. What remains is a clear record of which routes do not work.

u^{2} + 	frac94 - C igr)$, the second form for a composite on the principal series $w = -	frac32 \pm I_4
u$ (numbers are read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_4\}$). Hence $B_{\Lambda} 
eq 0$ exactly when $m^{2} > \Lambda C/3$, which for $C$ of order one is every composite heavier than the Hubble scale, and the flat bracket $ r{\pi^{1}\pi^{2}}$ is then nonzero up to the $\Lambda$-suppressed $\omega$-area.

The identity is a rewriting of the join and says nothing about a vacuum: it gives, at consistency level, the equation a broken phase must satisfy, without the potential that selects the phase, the $W$ and $Z$ masses or the weak mixing angle. families.bracket-fixed-join.lay: With a positive cosmological constant, the framework has an exact formula for the mass of a particle made of two conformal spinors. Turned around, the formula fixes the size of a quantity called the bracket and shows that, for typical values of the remaining invariant, it cannot vanish for anything heavier than the scale of cosmic expansion. Read at observation level only, alongside the bracket's charges, that looks like the signature of a condensate, similar in shape to the Higgs field's value, though what it would be a condensate of is left open. The result itself is only a rewriting, at consistency level: it does not choose a vacuum or predict the W and Z masses.

__notes__.note.families.abstract: A massive unit is two twistors and the maximal composite three (a bound imported at observation level), so there are three faces, with identical fermion content exchanged by $S_{3}$ and mixing by shared slots; that the faces are the generations is a conjecture. The mass bracket is fixed by the exact join, $2|B_{\Lambda}|^{2} = m^{2} - \Lambda C/3$, with a $\Lambda$-linear source; its magnitude cannot reach the weak scale (the thirteenth refutation), and under the indifference principle its direction is democratic, which under the Gram-square reading gives one heavy family and a Cabibbo check passed. The second half confronts the Koide relation. With $\sqrt{m}$ as the candidate linear coordinate, $Q_{\sqrt{m}} = 2/3$ says the family vector is null for the Minkowski member of the $S_{3}$-invariant forms; the framework does not force that member, and the $2\pi/3$ phases are Fourier coordinates, not a derivation. The Gaussian computation is proved in full: the pairing sector of the six-mode face algebra is one Bogoliubov event, the mass form is exactly rank one plus an ordering-shift floor with the light pair degenerate at every strength, and Koide survives only at a depth that is its own number transcribed. The displaced-Gaussian class is solved, by theorem for its pairings and by flagged computation for the rest; the split, the angle, and the depth are one open problem. The paper is Tier C; its lepton sector carries Hypothesis (S); every identity, the Wick evaluation included, is verified in exact arithmetic by a deposited script.
__notes__.note.families.setting-introduction:
The Standard-Model paper of this series derives one generation: the gauge algebra, the global group and the quark doublet with its hypercharge unconditionally, and the lepton doublet with the uniqueness of the hypercharge spectrum under a declared premise, Hypothesis (S) \cite{ButlerT12}. This paper asks why there are three, why one is heavy, and what the framework can and cannot say about the numbers. Its answers are of deliberately mixed strength, and the mixture is the point: this is the series' declared Tier C paper, and its most rigorous content is negative.

The affirmative results first. The maximal composite is three twistors, a bound the Standard-Model paper states at observation level and this paper imports at that level; a massive matter unit is two; so, given the bound, there are $\binom{3}{2} = 3$ ways to choose which two twistors carry the mass, and the conjecture, stated as a conjecture, is that the three generations are the three two-twistor faces of the maximal composite. What is proved outright, given the bound: the three faces carry identical fermion content, exchanged by $S_{3}$, and any two faces share exactly one twistor slot, so inter-family mixing is single-slot overlap, which at observation level is the CKM shape. The mass bracket is then fixed, not by a dynamics but by the exact join of the mass paper: $2|B_{\Lambda}|^{2} = m^{2} - \Lambda C/3$, so the deformed bracket of every composite heavier than the Hubble scale is nonzero. The join supplies a $\Lambda$-linear source term for the flat bracket, and the alignment computation delivers the thirteenth refutation and its redirection: the source cannot reach the weak scale (excluded by between forty-four and one hundred and five orders), but its \emph{direction} is $\Lambda$-independent, and under the indifference principle it is democratic, so that the leading mass form, read as a Gram square, is rank one and the third family's dominance is structural. Perturbations about democracy are nearest-neighbour textures, whose classic Cabibbo consequence $\theta_{C} \approx \sqrt{m_{d}/m_{s}} \approx 0.22$ passes at the percent level. Whether the condensate is an electroweak order parameter is a question the Standard-Model paper leaves open and this paper does not close: the bracket has the quantum numbers of $e^{c}$, not of a weak doublet, and the breaking language below is used at observation level only.

The second half confronts the framework's most precise numerical target: the Koide relation, $Q_{\sqrt{m}} = \sum m_{k} / (\sum \sqrt{m_{k}})^{2} = 2/3$, satisfied by the charged leptons to two parts in $10^{6}$ and unexplained since 1982. The framework supplies a reading, and the reading is stated at its level: masses generated at second order make $\sqrt{m}$ the candidate linear face-space coordinate for the light pair; in that coordinate Koide is the statement that the family vector is \emph{null} for the Minkowski member of the two-parameter family of $S_{3}$-invariant quadratic forms; the natural complex-bilinear form on face space is Euclidean on real vectors and does not select that member, so the light-cone reading is a choice the paper records as a choice; and the empirical Koide parametrisation with its $2\pi/3$ phases is the Fourier coordinate system on the doublet plane, available to every real vector, so that the relation's content is one number, the ratio $|\Gamma|^{2} = 2a^{2}$. Then the negative results. The six-mode Gaussian computation, proved here in full with its Wick evaluation printed and machine-checked, establishes the leading structure completely: the entire antisymmetric pairing sector is rigidly one Bogoliubov event, the mass form is exactly rank one plus an ordering-shift floor (the light families' masses are the ordering shift alone), and the light pair is degenerate everywhere in the class. It equally establishes the negative: the $S_{2} \to 1$ split is identically zero in the Gaussian class, Koide survives in the class only at a freezing depth that is Koide's own number transcribed ($x^{*} = (4+3\sqrt{2})^{4}/6 - 1/(6(1+x^{*})) = 769.33$), and the candidate inventory for the splitting is excluded (a closure theorem for the pairing sector; and, at the level of flagged preliminary computation, arithmetic for the noise channel and a relabelling conclusion for the condensate means). The terminal state as it stands is a classification: the displaced-Gaussian class is solved, its output is the skeleton plus bounded noise plus free textures that are the data under another name, and the split ($207$), the angle ($45^{\circ}$), and the depth ($769$) are one open problem in three forms, with the non-Gaussian completion the registered open problem.

(2) The condensation chain: the bracket fixed by the exact join, the $\Lambda$-linear source, the thirteenth refutation and the democratic alignment with its rank-one texture, and the Cabibbo check, each at its declared level (the section “Condensation and the ordering”). (3) The Koide geometry: the $\sqrt{m}$ coordinate, the nullity reformulation for the Minkowski member, the two-parameter invariant family and what the bracket form does and does not select, and the Fourier reading of the Koide parametrisation (the section “The Koide geometry”). (4) The Gaussian theorems: rigidity, rank one plus the ordering shift with the Wick evaluation in closed form, the unbreakable $S_{2}$, the depth $769.33$, and the classification of the class, by theorem for its pairings and by flagged computation for its noise channel and means (the section “The Gaussian theorems”). (5) The terminal state: one open problem in three forms, the registered open problem, and the closure of the absolute scale's map of failed routes by a covariance argument resting on an observation-level premise (the section “The terminal state”). (6) The weight spectrum's order of operations: the $126$ doublet direction of the module with its Georgi-Jarlskog Clebsch (the species under Hypothesis (S)), and, against the Standard-Model paper's no-go theorems, the reversal that puts the two-term structure first and the family breaking second, with the levels of the results (the section “The weight spectrum: the order of operations”). __notes__.note.mass.what-join-says: Two readings of one number, the first of them a definition, and beside them a field-side number that differs from it. On the composite side, the momentum is the grip on the frozen point, $P = M(I_{\Lambda})$, and mass is its length (Definition \claimref{obj.mass.grip-mass-composite}, a definition; Theorem \claimref{mass.exact-join} is the closed form of that length). On the representation side, that squared length is $Q(I)$ times the difference between the conformal Casimir and the de Sitter Casimir (Proposition \claimref{mass.casimir-form-join}): the part of the composite's conformal charge that the frozen point breaks. On the field side, mass is a weight read against the frozen point (Theorem \claimref{mass.mass-weight-dictionary}), and the composite's squared de Sitter mass is $-H^{2}C_{2}(I_{\Lambda}^{\perp})$, with $H^{2} = Q(I_{\Lambda}) = \Lambda/3$; it differs from the squared grip $Q(P)$ by $H^{2}C_{2}(\Lambda^{2}\CS)$, and the two agree only where the conformal Casimir vanishes. The flat-space formula is the leading term of \claimref{mass.exact-join}, and the correction is one term, $\tfrac{\Lambda}{3}C$, with $C$ the internal $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ Casimir of the pair: it depends on the constituents only through the imbalance of their helicities and their Hermitian overlap, and it vanishes exactly when the Gram matrix is scalar. The massless composites, for $\Lambda > 0$, are exactly those with $B_{\Lambda} = 0$ and scalar Gram matrix, a locus that is neither empty nor the doubled locus (Theorem \claimref{mass.exact-join}(5)), so compositeness by itself sets no lower bound on mass; the families paper has since settled the question this remark left open, fixing the bracket by the join and identifying the condensation seed as the source term, the $\Lambda$-linear tilt of the mass functional, rather than as a point of the massless locus \cite[Props.~4.1-4.2]{ButlerT13}. The point-supported evaluation, $B_{\Lambda} = \sigma(x)\br{\pi^{1}\pi^{2}}$, is the point of contact with the classical picture: for a composite localised at $x$ the deformed bracket is the flat one rescaled by the de Sitter conformal factor, which is what a conformally invariant pairing must do. Finally, the join fixes the units of Remark \claimref{note.mass.what-dictionary-does-does-not-yield}: the imaginary weight of a composite with $|B_{\Lambda}| \gg H\sqrt{C}$ is $\sqrt{2}|B_{\Lambda}|/H$ at leading order, the symplectic area of the misalignment in Hubble units.
__notes__.note.mass.point-contact-what-gravity-why: Assembling this paper with the action paper gives the following account, each claim at its declared level. First: mass is coupling to the frozen point, at theorem level for fields (Theorem \claimref{mass.mass-weight-dictionary}) and, for composites, by Definition \claimref{obj.mass.grip-mass-composite} with the closed form of Theorem \claimref{mass.exact-join}; and gravity's action is the MacDowell-Mansouri functional of the frozen point (Fact \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector}, whose action clause rests on an identity imported at assembly level). So matter and gravity are two relations to the same object: a massive field couples to $I$; gravity is the dynamics of $I$. Second, a structural reading of the equivalence principle: every mass term in the theory is a coupling to the one frozen point whose dynamics is the gravitational field, so the universality of gravitation, that gravitational and inertial mass coincide and everything falls alike, reads as the statement that the theory contains a single scale-giving object. Fields differ in how strongly they couple to $I$ (their weight), never in what they couple to. This is a reading, not a theorem: it rests on the two theorem-level ends and on the uniqueness of the scale-giving object, and it is entered in the levels of the results below at that level. Third, imported from the action paper at the levels it assigns: the action paper leaves the graviton's ontology open and states its engineering conclusion on either reading; on the reading in which the graviton is a collective mode of the boundary mode space, the acoustic no-go gives that conclusion at the mixed level of its inputs, one step conditional on the entropy paper's premise \cite[\S\S5--6]{ButlerT10}. Last, at the level of flagged speculation: a massive body is a multi-spinor composite (a composite of many conformal spinors), misaligned within (Proposition \claimref{mass.mass-symplectic-area-two-twistor-formula}) and coupled to $I$ through its grip (Definition \claimref{obj.mass.grip-mass-composite}, Theorem \claimref{mass.exact-join}), and its gravitational field is the response of the boundary mode space to that disturbance. In one sentence: gravity, at the quantum level, is the collective dynamics of the frozen point, coupling to which defines every mass, and everything falls the same way because there is only one point at infinity to couple to.

__notes__.note.mass.setting-grip-composite-frozen-: Three properties follow at once. First, $\ip{P}{I} = M_{I\wedge I} = 0$: the grip lies in $I^{\perp}$. Second, $m^{2}$ is invariant under the stabiliser of $I$: for $\gamma$ with $\gamma I = I$, $\ip{P(\gamma Z)}{U} = M_{U\wedge I}(\gamma Z) = M_{\gamma^{-1}(U\wedge I)}(Z) = M_{\gamma^{-1}U\wedge I}(Z) = \ip{P(Z)}{\gamma^{-1}U} = \ip{\gamma P(Z)}{U}$, so $P(\gamma Z) = \gamma P(Z)$ and $Q(P)$ is unchanged; for the frozen point of Lemma \claimref{mass.de-sitter-scale-frozen-point} the stabiliser acts on the ambient space through $SO(1,4)$ (Fact \claimref{mass.imported-frozen-point-tractor-connection}; the Lie-algebra form of the surjection is Lemma \claimref{mass.five-broken-generators}), and $P$ is a de Sitter vector. Third, at $\Lambda = 0$, $I = n_{\infty}$ and $\ip{P}{x} = M_{x\wedge n_{\infty}}$ is, by Lemma \claimref{mass.chart-form-spin-isomorphism}(2), the value of the translation generator on the composite, that is, its total momentum in the direction $x$; the $x$-slot part of $P$ is therefore the momentum, the remaining part is $-d\,n_{\infty}$ with $d$ the dilation charge, and since $n_{\infty}$ is null and orthogonal to the $x$-slot, $m^{2}$ is the Poincar\'e Casimir $p^{2}$. Definition \claimref{obj.mass.grip-mass-composite} is the de Sitter extension of the mass of Proposition \claimref{mass.mass-symplectic-area-two-twistor-formula}: the composite's momentum is its grip on the point at infinity, and its mass is the length of that grip. Lemma \claimref{mass.five-broken-generators} below identifies the generators $A(e_{a}\wedge I)$, $e_{a} \in I^{\perp}$, whose charges are the components of $P$, with the five generators of $\mathfrak{su}(2,2)$ broken by $I$, the de Sitter translations, which is the representation-theoretic form of the same statement. That $P$ is a real vector, so that $Q(P)$ is a value of the real $(1,4)$ form on $I^{\perp}$, is the next lemma.

__notes__.note.mass.point-contact-angle-between-tw: The correspondence paper proves that a conformal spinor (a twistor) is a state of the completion's three ladder pairs, a pure spinor, and that each conformal spinor determines a Fock vacuum \cite[Thm.~5.3]{ButlerT9}. __notes__.note.mass.setting-exact-join: Theorem \claimref{mass.mass-weight-dictionary} and Proposition \claimref{mass.mass-symplectic-area-two-twistor-formula} both compute a mass. __notes__.note.mass.what-dictionary-does-does-not-: The natural conjecture, that coupling to the frozen point explains the observed masses, fails quantitatively, and the failure is the finding. The unit is $H \approx 1.5 \times 10^{-33}\,\mathrm{eV}$, so the fields with real weight in $[-3,0]$, the complementary series with its endpoints, end at $m = 3H/2$, below every known massive particle. Every known massive field is in the principal series, with $\mathrm{Re}\,w = -\tfrac32$ and $\mathrm{Im}\,w = \nu \approx m/H$, about $3 \times 10^{38}$ for the electron. The dictionary does not remove the hierarchy problem; it restates it: the hierarchy is the question of why the imaginary parts of the conformal weights of matter are so large in Hubble units. What the dictionary does yield: a single origin for mass and dark energy, both couplings to $I$; the de Sitter representation theory of matter as its $w$-classification, with the $-\tfrac32$ of the principal series read as the universal real part of every weight; and, together with the area formula of the section “Mass as symplectic area”, a two-scale structure for the matter programme: the frozen point supplies the unit, the spinor bracket supplies the compositeness, and the internal symmetry of the multi-spinor system (many conformal spinors) is where the forces arise, taken up by the standard-model paper \cite{ButlerT12}.
__notes__.note.mass.point-contact-dictionary-plain: The universe, in this framework, has exactly one built-in scale: the length of the point at infinity, which is the cosmological constant under another name. The theorem says that mass is how strongly a field is coupled to that one scale: each field carries a number, its weight, and its mass is that number read against that single scale. A massless field is one whose weight gives zero mass against that scale. Against the data the natural conjecture fails: the scale is the Hubble scale, whose length is cosmological, so a field whose weight is an ordinary real number is lighter than anything ever observed, and everyday particles must carry weights whose imaginary part is extremely large. The mechanism does not explain why matter is so heavy compared to dark energy; it converts that question into a new one, which is the old hierarchy problem restated. The next section adds the other half of the account from the conformal spinor side, and the section “The exact join” joins the two halves.
__notes__.note.mass.setting-machine-verification:
Every computational identity asserted in this paper has been verified in exact arithmetic by the script \texttt{verify\_T11.py} \cite{ButlerVerifyT11}, which imports the series' shared library \texttt{GA.py}: exact rationals and Gaussian rationals, exact rank, rational functions in a formal variable, and exact truncated power series. No floating point is used anywhere; thirty-nine checks, all passing, organised in five parts keyed to statement tags.

\emph{Part A: the dictionary.} The pairing $I \cdot D\sigma$ is formed slot by slot from Facts \claimref{mass.imported-frozen-point-tractor-connection} and \claimref{mass.imported-thomas-operator}, with $\sigma$ and $\Box\sigma$ as formal coordinates, and $m^{2}$ is read off the resulting Klein-Gordon equation: $m^{2} = -w(w+n-1)Q(I)$ on a $144$-point rational grid in $(w, n, J)$, with a separate check that the opposite sign fails at every grid point where $m^{2} \neq 0$; in $n = 4$, $Q(I) = \Lambda/3$, $\rho_{I} = \Lambda/6$ and $m^{2} = -w(w+3)\Lambda/3$ as rational-function identities in a formal $\Lambda$. Corollary \claimref{mass.weight-polynomial-two-series}: the conformally coupled scalar's $m^{2} = 2\Lambda/3$ from the pairing; the massless weights $w = 0$ and $w = 1-n$, and no others among four further test values; the shadow symmetry $m^{2}(w) = m^{2}(1-n-w)$ and the closed form $\tfrac{n(n-2)}{4}Q(I)$ at $w = 1 - n/2$ for four values of $n$; the completed square $-w(w+3) = \tfrac94 - (w+\tfrac32)^{2}$ as a polynomial identity, with $m^{2} \ge 0$ at six real weights inside $[-3,0]$ and $m^{2} < 0$ at six outside; and $w = -\tfrac32 \pm I_4\nu$ (numbers read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_4\}$, the Gaussian rationals standing for $\mathbb{Q}(I_4)$) solving the dictionary in exact Gaussian rationals.

\emph{Part B: the area.} On exact Gaussian-rational spinor instances: a single twistor's momentum is null; $p^{2} = 2|\br{\pi^{1}\pi^{2}}|^{2}$ on all ten pairs with the imaginary part identically zero; aligned spinors give a null composite.

\emph{Part C: the chart and the de Sitter scale.} The chart on $\Lambda^{2}\C^{4}$: $\ip{n_{0}}{n_{\infty}} = +1$ with both null; $Q(x) = -2\det x$ and the orthogonality of the slots; $Q(X_{c}) = Q(1+2c)$ with $c$ undetermined (Remark \claimref{note.mass.what-nullity-fixes}). Lemma \claimref{mass.de-sitter-scale-frozen-point}: every slot of the flat tractor connection on $(\sigma, \nabla\sigma, -\tfrac14\Box\sigma)$ vanishes and the norm is $\Lambda/3$, as rational-function identities in $\Lambda$ at rational points; $\ip{X(x)}{n_{\infty} + \lambda n_{0}} = 1 - \lambda Q/2$ at rational points and three values of $\lambda$, with the inverted order giving $\lambda - Q/2$, and the six point embeddings of the uniqueness argument of exact rank six; the ambient pairing of $n_{\infty} + \lambda n_{0}$ with itself formed and equal to $2\lambda$ at four values, with $2\lambda = \Lambda/3$, and the vector null, hence simple by Fact \claimref{mass.imported-flat-model-twistor-chart-infinity}, exactly at $\lambda = 0$. Theorem \claimref{mass.exact-join}(1) and (4): both blocks of the deformed bracket on all ten twistor pairs, the assembled $B_{\Lambda}$ at $\Lambda = 3$, the point-supported factor $\sigma(x)$ at two points and two values of $\Lambda$, and the wedge identity $Z^{1}\wedge Z^{2} = \br{\pi^{1}\pi^{2}}X(x)$ for twistors built on the incidence line $\mu_{x}\pi + \pi$, at four points and two spinor pairs.

\emph{Part D: the grip theorem.} The spin isomorphism is solved exactly: for each rotation $R_{U\wedge V}$ the construction needs, the script finds the traceless $A$ whose action on every basis bivector equals that of the rotation. The nine rotations whose matrices Lemma \claimref{mass.chart-form-spin-isomorphism} displays (the grading, four translations, four special conformal generators) are compared with these solutions entry by entry. The moment map $M_{A}(Z^{1}, \dots, Z^{N}) := i\sum_{i=1}^{N} \bar{Z}^{i}\cdot(A Z^{i}), \qquad A \in \mathfrak{sl}(\T)$ and the grip of Definition \claimref{obj.mass.grip-mass-composite} are then built from these solutions, on ten twistor pairs: at $\Lambda = 0$, $Q(P) = 2|\br{\pi^{1}\pi^{2}}|^{2}$ and $P \perp n_{\infty}$; the grip on $n_{0}$, $M(n_{0})$, has squared length $2|[\omega^{1}\omega^{2}]|^{2}$; the cross term $\ip{P_{\infty}}{P_{0}}$ equals $p\cdot k - d^{2}$ with the three forms in the components of the proof, $\det t = \overline{\br{\pi^{1}\pi^{2}}}[\omega^{1}\omega^{2}]$, and equals $2\,\mathrm{Re}(\br{\pi^{1}\pi^{2}}\overline{[\omega^{1}\omega^{2}]}) + C$; and the theorem itself, $Q(P) = 2|B_{\Lambda}|^{2} + 2\lambda C$, as an identity in $\lambda$ (all three coefficients of the quadratic), with $m^{2}$ real, $P \perp I_{\Lambda}$, and $P_{\Lambda} = P_{\infty} + \lambda P_{0}$ recomputed independently at three values of $\lambda$. The identities for $C$ in the relation displayed with \claimref{mass.grip-real} and its nonnegativity. Lemma \claimref{mass.grip-real}: on four real points of the slice \claimref{note.mass.what-nullity-fixes}, every generator of a real pair (grading, translations, special conformal, Lorentz) has $\Sigma A$ anti-Hermitian, the commutator identity of the proof holds on all sixteen pairs of points, and the grip on $I_{\Lambda}$ has real pairing with $n_{\infty}$, $n_{0}$ and the four real vectors on all ten pairs, and the anti-Hermiticity condition on the eight real parameters of $x$ has rank four (Remark \claimref{note.mass.what-nullity-fixes}). Proposition \claimref{mass.casimir-form-join}: both Casimirs formed from the exact moment components in adapted bases, the decomposition (1), the value (2) and the closed form (3) on four pairs, and $\tr\mathsf{E}^{2} = 1$ on the grading element. \emph{Part E: the weight.} $\nu^{2} = 6|B_{\Lambda}|^{2}/\Lambda + C - \tfrac94$ on three pairs at two values of $\Lambda$, real and positive there; the expansion $\sqrt{1 - \tfrac94\epsilon^{2}} = 1 - \tfrac98\epsilon^{2} - \tfrac{81}{128}\epsilon^{4} + \cdots$, $\epsilon = H/m$, as an exact truncated power series.

What the script does not check: the conformal invariance of the Thomas operator (imported, Fact \claimref{mass.imported-thomas-operator}); the flat-model dictionary and the spin isomorphism as theorems (imported, Fact \claimref{mass.imported-flat-model-twistor-chart-infinity}; the script solves the isomorphism on the basis but does not prove it is one); Schur's lemma behind Lemma \claimref{mass.invariant-forms-simple-lie-algebra} (imported); the de Sitter classification against which Corollary \claimref{mass.weight-polynomial-two-series} is read (imported, Fact \claimref{mass.imported-unitary-representations-de-sitter-group}); the ``only if'' of the massless locus in Theorem \claimref{mass.exact-join}(5), which is the positivity argument of the proof; the normalisation $1/\sqrt2$ of the real slice \claimref{note.mass.what-nullity-fixes}, which the script carries as a scalar; the identification of the real form in Lemma \claimref{mass.five-broken-generators} (that the stabiliser is $\mathfrak{so}(1,4)$, that the five are the de Sitter translations, and the match with the action paper's Goldstone count), the script working over the Gaussian rationals, with no real-form check beyond the anti-Hermiticity checks of Lemma \claimref{mass.grip-real}; the $N$-constituent formulas of successor problem (5); and Proposition \claimref{mass.casimir-form-join}(2) beyond $N = 2$.
__notes__.note.neutrino.point-contact-why-neutrino: Every other fermion of the derived content has at least one pair mode occupied and is charged under something; the neutrino's right-handed partner is the one state with no mode occupied and nothing to be charged under: the empty pair system, the total singlet. The physics the seesaw needs (a fermion whose mass term requires no condensate) is exactly what a total singlet has in any gauge theory (a neutral bilinear with itself), and the section “The seesaw, and its premises” turns that match into the mechanism as far as gauge invariance can carry it, which is not as far as the framework's own bracket goes: that bracket is computed only on slot-occupying states, and T12 declares it undefined for an excited composite and says nothing about slot-free states (Fact \claimref{neutrino.imported-mass-bracket-quantum-numbers}), so the framework has not yet said which of its objects, if any, is the neutral bilinear of two grade-zero states. The reading explains the Standard Model's ambivalence, and Proposition \claimref{neutrino.empty-twistor}(2) makes the explanation exact: a bottom-up construction has only anomaly cancellation to fix hypercharges, and anomaly cancellation is insensitive to a fourth singlet, so it can neither require nor forbid $\nu_{R}$ nor fix its charge; a top-down content derivation computes the state and its weight, and carries it necessarily.
__notes__.note.neutrino.setting-successor-problems: Five. (1) \emph{The PMNS numbers:} all three angles are second-order effects here, depending on the same breaking that the CKM numbers depend on, and therefore on the families paper's second-order programme and its registered open problem \cite[Prop.~4.3(4), Obs.~7.1]{ButlerT13}; the large angles are the most demanding requirement on that breaking. (2) \emph{The two light masses and $\alpha$ at second order:} compute how far the two stages of the breaking lift $m_{2}$ and $m_{1}$, and what fixes $\alpha$, which would decide Premise (H), test the relation of Remark \claimref{note.neutrino.branch-m-3}, and convert the double-beta values into a single prediction; on the Standard-Model paper's Pati-Salam route the question becomes whether the family structure that fits the charged fermions there gives this branch. (3) \emph{Deriving $M$:} identify the framework's object that realises the neutral bilinear (Fact \claimref{neutrino.imported-mass-bracket-quantum-numbers} says nothing about it: the bracket is computed there only on slot states) and obtain its scale from its own dynamics rather than from the observed masses under Hypothesis (U), discharging Premise (M), deciding Premise (R), and turning the agreement with the dark-matter paper's rung scale from a construction into a check. (4) \emph{The degenerate pair and the non-thermal injection:} compute the split and widths of $N_{\perp}$ after the breaking, and bound the injected asymmetry ($\delta^{2}\sin\varphi$ from $N_{u'}$, $O(\sin\varphi)$ from the pair) from the descent's own dynamics rather than from the real-breaking assumption, which would convert the fifth stance from conditional to derived. (5) \emph{Dataset currency:} this paper's numbers are date-stamped by construction; the prediction table above is the object to refresh, and the capstone maintains the series-wide version.

__notes__.note.standard-model.setting-what-not-der: Theorem \claimref{standard-model.grip-mass-two-rung-module} settles what the frozen point does with the slot/pair distinction. This section asks whether anything else the series defines could set a slot-mode mass apart from a pair-mode mass in the demanded direction, and classifies what such an object would have to be.

At observation level, and flagged as such: if the pair mixing $U(3)$ were the colour group acting on the same ambient vector the frozen point lies in, Proposition \claimref{standard-model.frozen-point-pair-mixing} would say that mass breaks colour to a $U(2)$, which is false of the world. This paper does not make that identification: Proposition \claimref{standard-model.connection-forced} has the gauge algebra acting on a hierarchy bundle $\mathcal{H}$ of rank six, tensored with the local twistor bundle $\mathcal{S}$ on which the conformal connection acts, so the colour $SU(3)$ of Theorem \claimref{standard-model.gauge-algebra-minimal-massive-composite} acts on a factor to which the frozen point is insensitive. the section “The two flags, resolved” shows that the identification is not available in the first place: the pair mixing of the twistor's own Fock space is neither a spacetime symmetry nor an internal one, so it cannot be colour, and the apparent tension is a confusion of two copies of $\C^{3}$. Nothing in the section “The frozen point is insensitive to the slots” depends on it: Theorems \claimref{standard-model.moment-map-grip-mass-are-insensitive} and \claimref{standard-model.grip-mass-two-rung-module} use only that the frozen point lies in $V$ and that $\so(V_{\C})$ acts on the pair factor, which is true in either reading.
__notes__.note.standard-model.setting-two-flags-re: Two objections could be raised against the section “The frozen point is insensitive to the slots”: that Proposition \claimref{standard-model.frozen-point-pair-mixing} makes mass break colour, and that a frozen point completed along with the algebra might carry rung components and so be sensitive to the slots after all. __notes__.note.standard-model.setting-modules-mass: \emph{Convention.} Throughout, $\Lambda$ is a pure number, $3Q(I)$ in the tractor metric with the scale slot normalised to $\sigma = 1$, the mass paper's convention; ``$\Lambda = 0$'' in Theorem \claimref{standard-model.grip-mass-two-rung-module} and ``of order $\Lambda$'' in Propositions \claimref{standard-model.transported-frozen-point-doublet-datum-not} and \claimref{standard-model.transported-frozen-point} are statements in that unit; it is in this unit, and only in it, that $\Lambda/3$ is compared with the coefficient one in the section “The frozen point, transported”; the script takes $\Lambda$ rational for the same reason.
__notes__.note.standard-model.0-what-massless-mean: Two clarifications. First, at $\Lambda > 0$ Theorem \claimref{standard-model.moment-map-grip-mass-are-insensitive} holds unchanged, the frozen point still being a vector of $V$, and Theorem \claimref{standard-model.grip-mass-two-rung-module} becomes: the grip mass of a slot-singlet state is the single-component value of Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-grip-area-casimir-form}(iv), $H^{2}$ times a difference of Casimirs of the conformal spinor representation (the twistor representation), a number of order $H^{2}$; so ``massless'' reads ``at the Hubble scale'', which for the purposes of the running between $M_{Z}$ and $M_{U}$ is the same thing. Second, the grip mass of a state is the mass of the composite whose state it is, the object the mass paper defines; reading the sectors of the module as the species of one generation is Proposition \claimref{standard-model.under-s-composites-state-space-spinor}'s reading under (S), and the theorem inherits that reading and adds none of its own. What it says in that reading is structural and exact: the framework's mass mechanism produces mass only where a state has two slot components to misalign, and the $SU(2)$-singlet species have one.
__notes__.note.standard-model.two-pairings-two-pat: The grip of Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-frozen-point-grip-thirteenth-refutation} is a sesquilinear moment, $\ip{\Psi}{A\Psi}$ for a Hermitian product form, and a rung component of the frozen point enters it through mixed bivectors that change slot and pair number by one each, joining $Q$ to all four singlets and $L$ to $u^{c}$ and $d^{c}$ only: not the Yukawa pattern. The mass term of a Weyl fermion is a bilinear, $\psi\psi$, and the object that couples two sixteens to a vector is the invariant bilinear $B(\psi, x\varphi)$ of Lemma \claimref{standard-model.invariant-pairing-five-modes}, through which the same rung component joins exactly the Yukawa pairs. The two are different objects and answer different questions: the grip gives the mass of a composite state, the pairing the mass term between two species. A rung component is Higgs-like in the second sense and not in the first, and the second is the sense in which the Standard Model's Higgs is a Higgs.
__notes__.note.standard-model.setting-internal-sym: At observation level, and flagged as such: the three groups of the ladder are the shapes of the electromagnetic, electroweak, and strong factors, appearing in the order of the constituent count at which they arise. At observation level, and flagged as such: the two-twistor mass parameter is a weak singlet with hypercharge one, so the framework ties the mass of the composite to the abelian factor alone, at the level of compositeness at which mass first exists. The Standard Model's own order parameter is an $SU(2)$ doublet of hypercharge one half, not this object; the relation between the two is not settled here, and the reading is recorded as a reading.
__notes__.note.standard-model.sixth-refutation-lad: The natural conjecture, that the ladder of Proposition \claimref{standard-model.internal-symmetry-ladder} is the Standard Model gauge group, fails structurally, and for the sixth time in the series (the capstone keeps the count \cite{ButlerT17}) the failure makes the question more precise. The ladder's three groups act on \emph{different sectors}, indexed by constituent number, whereas $SU(3) \times SU(2) \times U(1)$ acts on all matter simultaneously as a direct product. What survives the refutation is the architecture: a fundamental matter unit built of up to three conformal spinors, each itself the vacuum of three pairs (Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-pair-systems-two-chirality-halves}), carries a two-level hierarchy of pairs, and the corrected conjecture is that the physical gauge group is the automorphism group of that hierarchy: the mixings respecting both levels of the partition. the section “The gauge algebra and the global form” proves the corrected conjecture's algebra and determines its global form; the representation content is the section “Content, charges, chirality”'s. Everything in this remark past the two propositions is at observation level, and is flagged as such.

__notes__.note.standard-model.setting-machine-veri:
Every computational identity asserted in this paper has been verified in exact arithmetic by the script \texttt{verify\_T12.py} \cite{ButlerVerifyT12}, which imports the series' shared library \texttt{GA.py}: exact rationals, Gaussian rationals with exact linear algebra over them, and arbitrary-precision integer arithmetic; the one field the library does not provide, the cyclotomic field $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_{6})$, is realised in the script in a few dozen lines. No floating point is used anywhere except in the lines marked RECORD (the GeV conversions, the proton lifetimes, and the two-loop integrations of Propositions \claimref{standard-model.supersymmetric-row-two-loops} and \claimref{standard-model.chain}, printed as records rather than checked) and in the checks marked CONTROL; two hundred and forty-three checks, all passing (two hundred and thirty-four exact, nine floating-point controls), organised in thirteen parts keyed to statement tags.

\emph{Part A: the ladder.} The polarisation step of Proposition \claimref{standard-model.internal-symmetry-ladder} at $n = 3$: the nine rank-one constraints $v^{\dagger}Mv = 0$ span the nine-dimensional real space of Hermitian forms on $\C^{3}$, so only $M = 0$ survives; and the nine products $\pi^{j}\bar\pi^{k}$ of an explicit three-twistor configuration have rank four, not nine, the dependence the proof must avoid (the $n = 2$ configuration has rank four of four). Exact rational unitaries (one real, one complex) are confirmed to preserve the total momentum; and the mass bracket is confirmed to transform by $\det(U)$ exactly on both, and to carry abelian weight $6$, hypercharge $+1$, under the generator of the section “Content, charges, chirality” (Proposition \claimref{standard-model.mass-bracket-charged-singlet}).

\emph{Part B: the algebra and the global form.} The action of an explicit $13$-generator basis of $\uu(2) \oplus \uu(3)$ on $\C^{2} \otimes \C^{3}$ has image of rank exactly $12$ by exact Gaussian-rational rank (the diagonal-phase kernel), and $\uu(3) \oplus \uu(3)$ on $\C^{3} \otimes \C^{3}$ has image rank $17$: the two dimension claims of Theorem \claimref{standard-model.gauge-algebra-minimal-massive-composite}. The coset rescaling law $\lambda^{2}\lambda^{-3} = \lambda^{-1}$ is confirmed on a unit-modulus Gaussian rational. In $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_{6})$: $\zeta_{6}$ has order exactly six, the second isomorphism $(a, b, \lambda) \mapsto (\lambda^{3}a, \lambda^{-2}b)$ evaluated on each of the six elements $(\zeta^{-3j}I_{2}, \zeta^{2j}I_{3}, \zeta^{j})$ returns the identity with $a$, $b$ of determinant one, and evaluated on $(I_{2}, I_{3}, \zeta)$ does not (that nothing else lies in the kernel is the determinant argument of the proof); and the lattice residue $2t + 3\delta + q \bmod 6$ vanishes on every representation of the section “Content, charges, chirality”, the hypercharge-zero singlet included, and does not vanish on a colour singlet of hypercharge $1/3$. The pair count $(n+2)/2$ equals three at $n = 4$ and at no other even $n$ in the tested range, and the algebra dimension $((n+2)/2)^{2} + 3$ equals twelve only there (Proposition \claimref{standard-model.four-dimensions-forces-converse}(1)); $m^{2} + k^{2} - 1 = 12$ has exactly the solutions $\{2, 3\}$ for $1 \le m, k \le 12$ (Proposition \claimref{standard-model.four-dimensions-forces-converse}(2)).

families.imported-dictionary-exact-join.formal:
Mass is conformal weight read against the frozen point: a density of weight $w$ coupled to the frozen point $I$ obeys the Klein-Gordon equation with $m^{2} = -w(w+3)\,\Lambda/3 = -w(w+3)H^{2}$. For the composite of two conformal spinors (twistors) the deformed bracket is $B_{\Lambda} = \br{\pi^{1}\pi^{2}} + \tfrac{\Lambda}{6}[\omega^{1}\omega^{2}]$ and the exact join is
\[
m^{2} \;=\; 2|B_{\Lambda}|^{2} + \frac{\Lambda}{3}\,C, \qquad C \ge 0,
\]
with $C$ the internal $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ Casimir of the pair, vanishing exactly when the Gram matrix of the two spinors is scalar; the massless composites for $\Lambda > 0$ are exactly those with $B_{\Lambda} = 0$ and scalar Gram matrix, and there are composites with $B_{\Lambda} = 0$ and $m^{2} = \Lambda C/3 \ne 0$. The induced weight of a composite heavier than $3H/2$ lies on the principal series, $w = -\tfrac32 \pm I_4\nu$ (numbers are read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_4\}$) with $\nu = m/H - \tfrac98 H/m + O((H/m)^{3})$: the mass sits in the imaginary part. \emph{Provenance:} \cite[Thm.~3.1, Thm.~5.6, Prop.~5.9]{ButlerT11}, with $C$ defined at \cite[eq.~(9)]{ButlerT11} and read in \cite[Rem.~5.10]{ButlerT11}.

families.imported-dictionary-exact-join.lay: This gathers two earlier results for later use. First, a field's mass is fixed by a number called its weight, read against the single scale that the cosmological constant provides. Second, a particle made of two conformal spinors has an exact mass formula: a term measuring how misaligned its parts are, plus a small correction proportional to the cosmological constant. For any ordinary particle the weight is a complex number whose imaginary part carries the mass.

proofs.main:
Mass is conformal weight read against the frozen point: a density of weight $w$ coupled to the frozen point $I$ obeys the Klein-Gordon equation with $m^{2} = -w(w+3)\,\Lambda/3 = -w(w+3)H^{2}$. For the composite of two conformal spinors (twistors) the deformed bracket is $B_{\Lambda} = \br{\pi^{1}\pi^{2}} + \tfrac{\Lambda}{6}[\omega^{1}\omega^{2}]$ and the exact join is
\[
m^{2} \;=\; 2|B_{\Lambda}|^{2} + \frac{\Lambda}{3}\,C, \qquad C \ge 0,
\]
with $C$ the internal $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ Casimir of the pair, vanishing exactly when the Gram matrix of the two spinors is scalar; the massless composites for $\Lambda > 0$ are exactly those with $B_{\Lambda} = 0$ and scalar Gram matrix, and there are composites with $B_{\Lambda} = 0$ and $m^{2} = \Lambda C/3 \ne 0$. The induced weight of a composite heavier than $3H/2$ lies on the principal series, $w = -\tfrac32 \pm I_4\nu$ (numbers are read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_4\}$) with $\nu = m/H - \tfrac98 H/m + O((H/m)^{3})$: the mass sits in the imaginary part. \emph{Provenance:} \cite[Thm.~3.1, Thm.~5.6, Prop.~5.9]{ButlerT11} (\claimref{mass.mass-weight-dictionary}, \claimref{mass.exact-join}, \claimref{mass.weight-composite}), with $C$ defined at \cite[eq.~(9)]{ButlerT11} and read in \cite[Rem.~5.10]{ButlerT11}.

families.imported-face-valued-bracket-qu.formal: A massive matter unit is a composite of two conformal spinors (twistors) whose flat mass is the bracket, $m^{2} = 2|\br{\pi^{1}\pi^{2}}|^{2}$ at $\Lambda = 0$. A fundamental matter unit is built of up to three conformal spinors, each the vacuum of three pairs; the three-spinor composite is the maximal one, and the Standard-Model paper states the bound at observation level, which is the level it has here. The mass bracket transforms by $\det(U)$ under the internal $U(2)$, an $SU(2)$ singlet with charge one under the determinant character, its modulus the mass and its phase pure gauge. Under the global form $S(U(2) \times U(3))$ with the hypercharge of the Standard-Model paper it transforms as $(1,1)$ with $Y = +1$: the quantum numbers of $e^{c}$, and not those of a weak doublet. The relation between this object and the Standard Model's order parameter, an $SU(2)$ doublet of hypercharge one half, is not settled in the series, and the reading of the bracket as an order parameter is recorded at observation level only. \emph{Provenance:} \cite[Prop.~4.1]{ButlerT11}; \cite[Rem.~3.3]{ButlerT12} for the three-spinor bound, at the observation level that remark declares (Thm.~4.1 there presupposes it in naming the maximal hierarchy); \cite[Props.~3.1-3.2]{ButlerT12} for the transformation law and the quantum numbers, with the level of the order-parameter sentence as stated there.
families.imported-face-valued-bracket-qu.technical:
A massive matter unit is a two-spinor composite with flat mass $m^{2} = 2|\br{\pi^{1}\pi^{2}}|^{2}$ at $\Lambda = 0$; a fundamental unit has up to three conformal spinors, each the vacuum of three pairs, and the three-spinor bound holds at observation level only. Under the internal $U(2)$ the bracket transforms by $\det(U)$: it is an $SU(2)$ singlet of charge one under the determinant character, with modulus the mass and phase pure gauge.

Under the global form $S(U(2) \times U(3))$ with the series' hypercharge, the bracket transforms as $(1,1)$ with $Y = +1$, the quantum numbers of $e^{c}$ and not those of a weak doublet. Its relation to the Standard Model's order parameter, an $SU(2)$ doublet of hypercharge one half, is not settled, and reading the bracket as an order parameter is an observation only.
families.imported-face-valued-bracket-qu.lay: In this framework a particle with mass is built from two conformal spinors, and its mass in flat space is carried by one complex number, the bracket. This result records how that number behaves under the framework's internal symmetries: it has the charges of $e^{c}$, the conjugate of the right-handed electron, with hypercharge $+1$, not those of the Higgs doublet of the Standard Model. Whether it nonetheless plays a role like the Higgs field is left open, and that reading is held at observation level only.

mass.casimir-form-join.technical:
For a composite with Hermitian Gram matrix $h$ and a nondegenerate subspace $W$ of the ambient space, $C_{2}(W)$ is the quadratic Casimir of the rotations of $W$ evaluated on the composite's moment components. For a nonzero non-null ambient vector $I$ with grip $P = M(I)$, the grip's length splits the conformal Casimir: $Q(P) = Q(I)\bigl(C_{2}(\Lambda^{2}\CS) - C_{2}(I^{\perp})\bigr)$, and the conformal Casimir is $C_{2}(\Lambda^{2}\CS) = \tr(h^{2}) - \tfrac14(\tr h)^{2}$ for any number of constituents.

For two conformal spinors, $I = I_{\Lambda}$ and $\Lambda \neq 0$, the de Sitter Casimir of the composite is $C_{2}(I_{\Lambda}^{\perp}) = \tfrac14(\tr h)^{2} + C - 6|B_{\Lambda}|^{2}/\Lambda$. These Casimirs are quadratic forms on moment components, and in this normalisation $C_{2}(I_{\Lambda}^{\perp})$ is the de Sitter Casimir of the scalar-module convention, acting as $-m^{2}/H^{2}$. So the grip equals the de Sitter mass plus $Q(I)$ times the conformal Casimir, and the two coincide only where the conformal Casimir vanishes, as on the massless locus, where $h = 0$.
mass.casimir-form-join.lay: The mass of a composite can be read in the language of symmetry. A composite carries charges under the whole conformal group and under the smaller de Sitter group picked out by the cosmological constant. Its mass squared is proportional to the difference between the two corresponding Casimir invariants: the part of its conformal charge that the cosmological scale breaks. This mass is not in general the mass read from the de Sitter symmetry alone: the two differ by the composite's conformal invariant times the cosmological scale, and agree only where that invariant vanishes.
mass.casimir-form-join.typing_note: Part (3) combines (1) and (2) with the exact join's mass formula, so the exact join was added; the E301 cycle with the invariant-forms lemma is broken on the lemma's side, and the de Sitter representation Fact is a normalisation comparison only.

proofs.main:
Conventions: the chart's complex unit is $I_{6}$, the complex unit of the conformal spinor space $\CS$, acting on conformal spinors by right multiplication; numbers formed from conformal spinors (values of the Hermitian form, components, traces) are read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{6}\}$, and the bar is the conjugation that reverses $I_{6}$.

(1) Take a basis $e_{1}, \dots, e_{5}$ of $I^{\perp}$ and $e_{6} = I$; then $g^{a6} = 0$ for $a \le 5$ and $g^{66} = 1/Q(I)$. In $\tfrac12 g^{\alpha\alpha'}g^{\beta\beta'}M_{\alpha\beta}M_{\alpha'\beta'}$ the terms with no index equal to $6$ sum to $C_{2}(I^{\perp})$; the terms with exactly one $6$ in $(\alpha,\beta)$ need exactly one $6$ in $(\alpha',\beta')$ in the matching position, giving $\tfrac12\bigl(g^{ab}g^{66}M_{a6}M_{b6} + g^{66}g^{ab}M_{6a}M_{6b}\bigr) = g^{66}g^{ab}M_{a6}M_{b6}$; terms with $\alpha = \beta = 6$ vanish since $M_{66} = 0$. Now $M_{a6} = M_{e_{a}\wedge I} = \ip{P}{e_{a}}$, and $P \in I^{\perp}$, so $g^{ab}\ip{P}{e_{a}}\ip{P}{e_{b}} = Q(P)$. Hence $C_{2}(\Lambda^{2}\CS) = C_{2}(I^{\perp}) + Q(P)/Q(I)$.

(2) \emph{The moment element.} Let $\mathsf{M} := \sum_{i}(Z^{i}I_{6})\otimes(\bar{Z}^{i}\cdot\,)$ be the endomorphism $W \mapsto \sum_{i}Z^{i}\,(\bar{Z}^{i}\cdot W)\,I_{6}$ of $\CS$, so that $M_{A} = \tr(\mathsf{M}A)$ by $M_{A}(Z^{1}, \dots, Z^{N}) := i\sum_{i=1}^{N} \bar{Z}^{i}\cdot(A Z^{i}), \qquad A \in \mathfrak{sl}(\T)$, and let $\mathsf{M}_{0}$ be its traceless part; since every $A_{\alpha\beta} := A(e_{\alpha}\wedge e_{\beta})$ is traceless, $M_{\alpha\beta} = \tr(\mathsf{M}_{0}A_{\alpha\beta})$.

\emph{An invariant form.} Put
\[
\Phi(A, B) := \tfrac12\, g^{\alpha\alpha'}g^{\beta\beta'}\,\tr(AA_{\alpha\beta})\,\tr(BA_{\alpha'\beta'})
\]
on $\mathfrak{sl}(\CS)$, so that $C_{2}(\Lambda^{2}\CS) = \Phi(\mathsf{M}_{0}, \mathsf{M}_{0})$. It is symmetric, and invariant: under $A \mapsto \gamma A\gamma^{-1}$ the matrices $A_{\alpha\beta}$ transform by the rotation of the ambient basis induced by $\gamma$ (Fact \claimref{mass.imported-flat-model-twistor-chart-infinity}), and the contraction with $g^{\alpha\alpha'}g^{\beta\beta'}$ is invariant under rotations of the basis. By Lemma \claimref{mass.invariant-forms-simple-lie-algebra}, $\Phi(A,B) = \kappa\tr(AB)$ for a constant $\kappa$.

\emph{The constant.} Evaluate at $A = B = \mathsf{E} := A(n_{\infty}\wedge n_{0}) = \operatorname{diag}(-\tfrac12,-\tfrac12,\tfrac12,\tfrac12)$, the grading element, in the basis $n_{\infty}, n_{0}$, $x$-slot. For a translation or special conformal generator $\tr(\mathsf{E}A_{\alpha\beta}) = 0$, the blocks being off-diagonal (Lemma \claimref{mass.chart-form-spin-isomorphism}). For a rotation of the $x$-slot: it annihilates $n_{\infty}$ and $n_{0}$, and an $A$ with $A\cdot n_{\infty} = 0$ has no $\Som \to \Spi$ block (the mixed component of $Ae_{1}\wedge e_{2} + e_{1}\wedge Ae_{2}$ is that block applied to $e_{1}, e_{2}$) and traceless $\Som$-block (the $n_{\infty}$-component is $\tr_{\Som}A$), and likewise from $n_{0}$; so $\tr(\mathsf{E}A_{\alpha\beta}) = -\tfrac12\tr_{\Som}A + \tfrac12\tr_{\Spi}A = 0$. Finally $\tr(\mathsf{E}\,A(n_{\infty}\wedge n_{0})) = \tr \mathsf{E}^{2} = 1$ and $\tr(\mathsf{E}\,A(n_{0}\wedge n_{\infty})) = -1$. With $g^{\infty 0} = g^{0\infty} = 1$ and $g^{\infty\infty} = g^{00} = 0$ the only surviving terms of $\Phi(\mathsf{E},\mathsf{E})$ are $(\alpha\beta, \alpha'\beta') = (\infty 0, 0\infty)$ and $(0\infty, \infty 0)$, each contributing $-1$, so $\Phi(\mathsf{E},\mathsf{E}) = -1 = \kappa\tr \mathsf{E}^{2} = \kappa$.

\emph{The value.} Hence $C_{2}(\Lambda^{2}\CS) = -\tr(\mathsf{M}_{0}^{2})$. Now $\tr\mathsf{M} = I_{6}\sum_{i}\bar{Z}^{i}\cdot Z^{i} = I_{6}\tr h$ and $\tr\mathsf{M}^{2} = -\sum_{i,l}(\bar{Z}^{i}\cdot Z^{l})(\bar{Z}^{l}\cdot Z^{i}) = -\tr(h^{2})$ ($h$ is Hermitian), so $-\tr(\mathsf{M}_{0}^{2}) = -\tr\mathsf{M}^{2} + \tfrac14(\tr\mathsf{M})^{2} = \tr(h^{2}) - \tfrac14(\tr h)^{2}$.

(3) Combine (1), (2) and \claimref{mass.exact-join}: $C_{2}(I_{\Lambda}^{\perp}) = \tr h^{2} - \tfrac14(\tr h)^{2} - C - 6|B_{\Lambda}|^{2}/\Lambda$, and $\tr h^{2} - \tfrac14(\tr h)^{2} - C = \tfrac12\tr h^{2} = \tfrac14(\tr h)^{2} + C$ by the relation displayed with \claimref{mass.grip-real}. The script forms both Casimirs from the exact moment components in adapted bases and confirms (1), (2) and (3) on four pairs, together with $\tr\mathsf{E}^{2} = 1$.

mass.exact-join.technical:
With the frozen point $I_{\Lambda} = n_{\infty} + \tfrac{\Lambda}{6}n_{0}$ and two conformal spinors $Z^{1}, Z^{2} \in \CS$, the pairing of the composite against the frozen point is the deformed bracket $B_{\Lambda} = \ip{I_{\Lambda}}{Z^{1}\wedge Z^{2}} = \br{\pi^{1}\pi^{2}} + \tfrac{\Lambda}{6}[\omega^{1}\omega^{2}]$. The grip $P = M(I_{\Lambda})$ has squared length $m^{2} = 2|B_{\Lambda}|^{2} + \tfrac{\Lambda}{3}C$, with $C$ the internal $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ Casimir of the Gram matrix $h$; at $\Lambda = 0$ this is the two-spinor area formula $m^{2} = 2|\br{\pi^{1}\pi^{2}}|^{2}$.

For two spinors on the line $L_{x}$ of a point $x$, $B_{\Lambda} = \bigl(1 - \Lambda Q(x)/12\bigr)\br{\pi^{1}\pi^{2}}$, the flat bracket read in the de Sitter scale. For $\Lambda > 0$, $m^{2} \ge 0$, with equality exactly when $B_{\Lambda} = 0$ and $h$ is a multiple of the identity, a multiple that is in fact zero ($h = 0$, proved in the many-constituent join); the doubled composite has $m^{2} = \tfrac{\Lambda}{3}(\bar{Z}\cdot Z)^{2}$, and there are massless composites that are not doubled.
mass.exact-join.lay: The framework reads mass in two ways: from how a composite grips the one built-in cosmological scale, and from how misaligned its two constituents are. This theorem joins the two readings exactly. The mass squared is twice the squared size of a slightly deformed misalignment, plus a tiny correction, proportional to the cosmological constant, that depends on how the constituents overlap. Without a cosmological constant the familiar two-constituent area formula returns.
mass.exact-join.typing_note: All five uses are cited in the proof and kept (the area formula for the flat-shadow clause); the grip definition was added under about, and the unresolved nullity remark is not a store entity.

proofs.main:
Conventions: the chart's complex unit is $I_{6}$, the complex unit of the conformal spinor space $\CS$, acting on conformal spinors by right multiplication; numbers formed from conformal spinors (values of the Hermitian form, components, traces) are read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{6}\}$, and the bar is the conjugation that reverses $I_{6}$; $\Som$ and $\Spi$ are the halves of $\CS$ spanned by $e_{1}, e_{2}$ and by $e_{3}, e_{4}$, the $E = -1$ and $E = +1$ eigenspaces.

(1) Expand $Z^{1}\wedge Z^{2} = (\omega^{1} + \pi^{1})\wedge(\omega^{2} + \pi^{2})$ into four terms. Pairing against $n_{\infty} = e_{1}\wedge e_{2}$ annihilates every term with an $\omega$ factor (the wedge repeats a vector of $\Som$), leaving $\varepsilon(e_{1}\wedge e_{2}\wedge\pi^{1}\wedge\pi^{2}) = \varepsilon_{a'b'}\pi_{1}^{a'}\pi_{2}^{b'}\,\varepsilon(e_{1}\wedge e_{2}\wedge e_{3}\wedge e_{4}) = \br{\pi^{1}\pi^{2}}$; pairing against $n_{0} = e_{3}\wedge e_{4}$ likewise leaves $\varepsilon(e_{3}\wedge e_{4}\wedge\omega^{1}\wedge\omega^{2}) = [\omega^{1}\omega^{2}]\,\varepsilon(e_{3}\wedge e_{4}\wedge e_{1}\wedge e_{2}) = [\omega^{1}\omega^{2}]$, the permutation being even. Linearity in $I_{\Lambda}$ gives \claimref{mass.exact-join}; at $\Lambda = 0$ the frozen point is $n_{\infty}$ (the infinity twistor) (Lemma \claimref{mass.de-sitter-scale-frozen-point}(3)).

(2) \emph{Slots of the grip.} $M_{U\wedge I}$ is linear in $U \wedge I$, so with $I_{\Lambda} = n_{\infty} + \lambda n_{0}$ the grip is $P = P_{\infty} + \lambda P_{0}$, where $P_{\infty} := M(n_{\infty})$ and $P_{0} := M(n_{0})$. Put $d := M_{n_{\infty}\wedge n_{0}}$, and for $x$ in the $x$-slot $p(x) := M_{x\wedge n_{\infty}}$, $k(x) := M_{x\wedge n_{0}}$, three linear forms in $x$. Then $\ip{P}{n_{\infty}} = M_{n_{\infty}\wedge I_{\Lambda}} = \lambda M_{n_{\infty}\wedge n_{0}} = \lambda d$, $\ip{P}{n_{0}} = M_{n_{0}\wedge n_{\infty}} = -d$, and $\ip{P}{x} = p(x) + \lambda k(x)$. Writing $P = \alpha n_{\infty} + \beta n_{0} + v$ with $v$ in the $x$-slot, $\alpha = \ip{P}{n_{0}} = -d$, $\beta = \ip{P}{n_{\infty}} = \lambda d$, and $\ip{v}{x} = p(x) + \lambda k(x)$ for all $x$. Hence
\[
Q(P) = 2\alpha\beta + Q(v) = -2\lambda d^{2} + Q(p) + 2\lambda\, p\cdot k + \lambda^{2}\, Q(k),
\]
where $f \cdot g$ denotes the dual metric on linear forms on the $x$-slot. By Remark \claimref{note.mass.what-nullity-fixes} the metric matrix on the $x$-slot, in the components $x^{aa'}$, is $G = -\varepsilon\otimes\varepsilon$; since $\varepsilon^{2} = -1$, $G^{2} = (\varepsilon\otimes\varepsilon)^{2} = \varepsilon^{2}\otimes\varepsilon^{2} = 1$, so $G^{-1} = G$ and $f\cdot g = -\varepsilon_{ab}\varepsilon_{a'b'}f_{aa'}g_{bb'}$ with the same numerical symbols. Below, $u\cdot v$ for two $2$-component objects is the plain sum $\sum_{a}u_{a}v_{a}$ of products of components.

\emph{The three forms in components.} By Lemma \claimref{mass.chart-form-spin-isomorphism}(2), $A(x\wedge n_{\infty})Z = b_{x}\pi \in \Som$, so by the relation displayed with \claimref{mass.chart-form-spin-isomorphism} and $M_{A}(Z^{1}, \dots, Z^{N}) := i\sum_{i=1}^{N} \bar{Z}^{i}\cdot(A Z^{i}), \qquad A \in \mathfrak{sl}(\T)$, $p(x) = I_{6}\sum_{i}\hp{\pi^{i}}{b_{x}\pi^{i}} = I_{6}\sum_{i} x^{aa'}\,\overline{\pi^{i}_{a}}\,(\varepsilon\pi^{i})_{a'}$, where $(\varepsilon\pi)_{a'} := \varepsilon_{a'b'}\pi^{b'}$ and $\overline{\pi^{i}_{a}}$ is the conjugate of the component of $\pi^{i}$ paired with $e_{a}$ by $\Sigma$. Thus $p = \sum_{i}p^{i}$ with $p^{i}_{aa'} = I_{6}\,\overline{\pi^{i}_{a}}\,(\varepsilon\pi^{i})_{a'}$. By Lemma \claimref{mass.chart-form-spin-isomorphism}(3), $A(x\wedge n_{0})Z = c_{x}\omega \in \Spi$, so $k(x) = I_{6}\sum_{i}\overline{\hp{c_{x}\omega^{i}}{\omega^{i}}} = I_{6}\sum_{i}\sum_{a'}(c_{x}\omega^{i})^{a'}\,\overline{\omega^{i}_{a'}} = -I_{6}\sum_{i}x^{ba'}\varepsilon_{ba}\omega^{i\,a}\,\overline{\omega^{i}_{a'}}$; thus $k = \sum_{i}k^{i}$ with $k^{i}_{aa'} = -I_{6}\,(\varepsilon\omega^{i})_{a}\,\overline{\omega^{i}_{a'}}$, where $(\varepsilon\omega)_{a} := \varepsilon_{ab}\omega^{b}$. By Lemma \claimref{mass.chart-form-spin-isomorphism}(1), $A(n_{\infty}\wedge n_{0})Z = (-\tfrac12\omega, \tfrac12\pi)$, so $\bar{Z}\cdot AZ = -\tfrac12\hp{\pi}{\omega} + \tfrac12\overline{\hp{\pi}{\omega}} = -I_{6}\,\mathrm{Im}\hp{\pi}{\omega}$ and $d = \sum_{i}\mathrm{Im}\,t_{ii} = \mathrm{Im}\tr t$.

\emph{The three pairings.} Using $\varepsilon^{\mathsf T}\varepsilon = 1$, $\varepsilon^{2} = -1$ and $\det\varepsilon = 1$ for the $2\times 2$ symbol:
\begin{align*}
p^{i}\cdot p^{l} &= -\varepsilon_{ab}\varepsilon_{a'b'}\,(I_{6})^{2}\,\overline{\pi^{i}_{a}}\,\overline{\pi^{l}_{b}}\,(\varepsilon\pi^{i})_{a'}(\varepsilon\pi^{l})_{b'}
= \overline{\br{\pi^{i}\pi^{l}}}\;\br{\varepsilon\pi^{i},\varepsilon\pi^{l}} = |\br{\pi^{i}\pi^{l}}|^{2},\\
k^{i}\cdot k^{l} &= -\varepsilon_{ab}\varepsilon_{a'b'}\,(-I_{6})^{2}\,(\varepsilon\omega^{i})_{a}(\varepsilon\omega^{l})_{b}\,\overline{\omega^{i}_{a'}}\,\overline{\omega^{l}_{b'}}
= [\varepsilon\omega^{i},\varepsilon\omega^{l}]\;\overline{[\omega^{i}\omega^{l}]} = |[\omega^{i}\omega^{l}]|^{2},\\
p^{i}\cdot k^{l} &= -\varepsilon_{ab}\varepsilon_{a'b'}\,(I_{6})(-I_{6})\,\overline{\pi^{i}_{a}}\,(\varepsilon\omega^{l})_{b}\,(\varepsilon\pi^{i})_{a'}\,\overline{\omega^{l}_{b'}}
= -\bigl(-\overline{\pi^{i}}\cdot\omega^{l}\bigr)\bigl(\pi^{i}\cdot\overline{\omega^{l}}\bigr) = t_{il}\,\overline{t_{il}} = |t_{il}|^{2},
\end{align*}
where in the last line $\varepsilon_{ab}u_{a}(\varepsilon v)_{b} = u^{\mathsf T}\varepsilon\varepsilon v = -u\cdot v$ and $\varepsilon_{a'b'}(\varepsilon u)_{a'}v_{b'} = u^{\mathsf T}\varepsilon^{\mathsf T}\varepsilon v = u\cdot v$. Summing over $i, l$: $Q(p) = 2|\br{\pi^{1}\pi^{2}}|^{2}$ (the diagonal terms vanish, and this is Proposition \claimref{mass.mass-symplectic-area-two-twistor-formula} again), $Q(k) = 2|[\omega^{1}\omega^{2}]|^{2}$, and $p\cdot k = \sum_{i,l}|t_{il}|^{2}$. Therefore
\[
Q(P) = 2|\br{\pi^{1}\pi^{2}}|^{2} + 2\lambda^{2}|[\omega^{1}\omega^{2}]|^{2} + 2\lambda\Bigl(\sum_{i,l}|t_{il}|^{2} - (\mathrm{Im}\tr t)^{2}\Bigr).
\]

\emph{The comparison.} $2|B_{\Lambda}|^{2} = 2|\br{\pi^{1}\pi^{2}}|^{2} + 2\lambda^{2}|[\omega^{1}\omega^{2}]|^{2} + 4\lambda\,\mathrm{Re}\bigl(\br{\pi^{1}\pi^{2}}\,\overline{[\omega^{1}\omega^{2}]}\bigr)$. The matrix $t$ is the product of the matrix with rows $\overline{\pi^{1}}, \overline{\pi^{2}}$ and the matrix with columns $\omega^{1}, \omega^{2}$, so $\det t = \overline{\br{\pi^{1}\pi^{2}}}\,[\omega^{1}\omega^{2}]$ and $\mathrm{Re}\det t = \mathrm{Re}\bigl(\br{\pi^{1}\pi^{2}}\overline{[\omega^{1}\omega^{2}]}\bigr)$. It remains to show
\[
\sum_{i,l}|t_{il}|^{2} - (\mathrm{Im}\tr t)^{2} - 2\,\mathrm{Re}\det t \;=\; C .
\]
With $h_{11} = 2\,\mathrm{Re}\,t_{11}$, $h_{22} = 2\,\mathrm{Re}\,t_{22}$, $h_{12} = t_{12} + \overline{t_{21}}$, the right side is $(\mathrm{Re}\,t_{11} - \mathrm{Re}\,t_{22})^{2} + |t_{12}|^{2} + |t_{21}|^{2} + 2\,\mathrm{Re}(t_{12}t_{21})$, and the left side is $|t_{11}|^{2} + |t_{22}|^{2} + |t_{12}|^{2} + |t_{21}|^{2} - (\mathrm{Im}\,t_{11} + \mathrm{Im}\,t_{22})^{2} - 2\,\mathrm{Re}(t_{11}t_{22}) + 2\,\mathrm{Re}(t_{12}t_{21})$. Their difference is
\[
|t_{11}|^{2} + |t_{22}|^{2} - (\mathrm{Im}\,t_{11} + \mathrm{Im}\,t_{22})^{2} - 2\,\mathrm{Re}(t_{11}t_{22}) - (\mathrm{Re}\,t_{11} - \mathrm{Re}\,t_{22})^{2},
\]
and writing $t_{jj} = r_{j} + I_{6} s_{j}$ this is $(r_{1}^{2} + s_{1}^{2} + r_{2}^{2} + s_{2}^{2}) - (s_{1} + s_{2})^{2} - 2(r_{1}r_{2} - s_{1}s_{2}) - (r_{1} - r_{2})^{2} = 0$. Hence $Q(P) = 2|B_{\Lambda}|^{2} + 2\lambda C$, and $2\lambda = Q(I_{\Lambda}) = \Lambda/3$ by Lemma \claimref{mass.de-sitter-scale-frozen-point}(3). The identities for $C$ in the relation displayed with \claimref{mass.grip-real} are the $2\times 2$ identities $\tr(h_{0}^{2}) = \tr h^{2} - \tfrac12(\tr h)^{2}$ and $\tr h^{2} = (\tr h)^{2} - 2\det h$.

(3) At $\lambda = 0$ the formula reduces to its first term, and (1) identifies $B_{0}$ with $\br{\pi^{1}\pi^{2}} = \ip{n_{\infty}}{Z^{1}\wedge Z^{2}}$.

(4) In the chart of Fact \claimref{mass.imported-flat-model-twistor-chart-infinity} the line of $x$ is the graph $L_{x} = \{\mu_{x}\pi + \pi : \pi \in \Spi\}$ of the map $\mu_{x}: \Spi \to \Som$, $(\mu_{x}\pi)^{a} = x^{aa'}\varepsilon_{b'a'}\pi^{b'}$, that is $\mu_{x} = -b_{x}$ in the notation of Lemma \claimref{mass.chart-form-spin-isomorphism} \cite[Thm.~4.2]{ButlerT9} (\claimref{correspondence.incidence-relation-chart}); indeed $(\mu_{x}e_{3} + e_{3})\wedge(\mu_{x}e_{4} + e_{4}) = n_{0} + \mu_{x}e_{3}\wedge e_{4} + e_{3}\wedge\mu_{x}e_{4} + \det(\mu_{x})\,n_{\infty} = n_{0} + x^{a4}e_{a}\wedge e_{4} + x^{a3}e_{a}\wedge e_{3} + \det(x^{aa'})\,n_{\infty} = X(x)$, since $\det\mu_{x} = \det(x^{aa'}) = -\tfrac12 Q(x)$ by Remark \claimref{note.mass.what-nullity-fixes}. Two conformal spinors on $L_{x}$ are $Z^{i} = \mu_{x}\pi^{i} + \pi^{i}$, and bilinearity with antisymmetry gives $Z^{1}\wedge Z^{2} = \pi_{1}^{a'}\pi_{2}^{b'}\,(\mu_{x}e_{a'} + e_{a'})\wedge(\mu_{x}e_{b'} + e_{b'}) = \br{\pi^{1}\pi^{2}}\,(\mu_{x}e_{3} + e_{3})\wedge(\mu_{x}e_{4} + e_{4}) = \br{\pi^{1}\pi^{2}}\,X(x)$. Then $B_{\Lambda} = \br{\pi^{1}\pi^{2}}\ip{I_{\Lambda}}{X(x)} = \br{\pi^{1}\pi^{2}}\,\sigma(x)$ by Lemma \claimref{mass.de-sitter-scale-frozen-point}(2).

(5) Both terms of \claimref{mass.exact-join} are nonnegative for $\Lambda > 0$, and $C = 0$ iff $h_{11} = h_{22}$ and $h_{12} = 0$. For $Z^{2} = Z^{1}$: $Z\wedge Z = 0$ gives $B_{\Lambda} = 0$; $h = h_{11}\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&1\\1&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ gives $C = \tfrac14\cdot 0 + h_{11}^{2}$. mass.five-broken-generators.formal: Let $\Omega_{I}(u,v) := \ip{I}{u\wedge v}$ be the $2$-form on the conformal spinor space $\CS$ (twistor space) of an ambient vector $I$; it is nondegenerate iff $I$ is non-simple iff $Q(I) \neq 0$. For such $I$, the elements $A \in \mathfrak{sl}(\CS)$ with $\Omega_{I}A$ symmetric form the stabiliser of $I$, of dimension $10$ (six conditions on $\mathfrak{gl}(\CS)$, none of which is the trace); the elements with $\Omega_{I}A$ antisymmetric form a $6$-dimensional complement in $\mathfrak{gl}(\CS)$, cut to $5$ by the trace; and the five generators $A(e_{a}\wedge I)$, $e_{a}$ a basis of $I^{\perp}$, are an independent basis of that $5$-dimensional complement. On the real form, for the frozen point with $\Lambda > 0$, the stabiliser is $\mathfrak{so}(1,4)$ and the five are the de Sitter translations, the $I$-half of the nine Goldstone modes of the action paper \cite[Prop.~5.4]{ButlerT10}.
mass.five-broken-generators.technical:
An ambient vector $I$ defines a $2$-form $\Omega_{I}(u,v) = \ip{I}{u\wedge v}$ on the conformal spinor space $\CS$, nondegenerate exactly when $Q(I) \neq 0$. For such $I$, the elements $A \in \mathfrak{sl}(\CS)$ with $\Omega_{I}A$ symmetric form the stabiliser of $I$, of dimension $10$; those with $\Omega_{I}A$ antisymmetric form a $6$-dimensional complement in $\mathfrak{gl}(\CS)$, cut to $5$ by the trace, and the five generators $A(e_{a}\wedge I)$, $e_{a}$ a basis of $I^{\perp}$, are an independent basis of it.

On the real form, for the frozen point with $\Lambda > 0$, the stabiliser is $\mathfrak{so}(1,4)$ and the five broken generators are the de Sitter translations, the $I$-half of the nine Goldstone modes of the action principle.
mass.five-broken-generators.lay: The cosmological scale picks out a direction that breaks the conformal symmetry of spacetime down to de Sitter symmetry. Of the fifteen conformal symmetries ten survive and five are broken. This result identifies the five broken ones exactly: they are the de Sitter translations, the symmetries whose charges make up a composite's momentum.
mass.five-broken-generators.typing_note: The proof relies on the pairing on bivectors and the isomorphism defining $A(U\wedge V)$, both from the flat-model Fact, so that Fact was added; the action paper's Goldstone count (context_ref) is a comparison and was not added.

proofs.main:
The components of $\Omega_{I}$ are $\varepsilon(I\wedge e_{k}\wedge e_{l})$, the Hodge dual of $I$, and its Pfaffian is a nonzero multiple of $\varepsilon(I\wedge I) = Q(I)$; so $\Omega_{I}$ is nondegenerate iff $Q(I) \neq 0$, which is the non-simplicity of $I$ (Lemma \claimref{mass.de-sitter-scale-frozen-point}(3)). For $A \in \mathfrak{gl}(\CS)$ put $\beta_{A}(u,v) := \Omega_{I}(u, Av) = u^{\mathsf T}\Omega_{I}Av$; since $\Omega_{I}^{\mathsf T} = -\Omega_{I}$, $\Omega_{I}(Au,v) = -\beta_{A}(v,u)$, so $\Omega_{I}(Au,v) + \Omega_{I}(u,Av) = \beta_{A}(u,v) - \beta_{A}(v,u)$, and $A$ preserves $\Omega_{I}$ iff $\beta_{A}$, that is the matrix $\Omega_{I}A$, is symmetric. By invariance of the pairing under the action of $\mathfrak{sl}(\CS)$ (Fact \claimref{mass.imported-flat-model-twistor-chart-infinity}), $\ip{I}{A\cdot(u\wedge v)} = -\ip{A\cdot I}{u\wedge v}$, so $\Omega_{I}(Au,v) + \Omega_{I}(u,Av) = -\Omega_{A\cdot I}(u,v)$: preserving $\Omega_{I}$ is the same as stabilising $I$, and the antisymmetric part of $\beta_{A}$ is $-\tfrac12\Omega_{A\cdot I}$. Symmetry of a $4\times 4$ matrix is six conditions, so the stabiliser is $10$-dimensional; it is $\mathfrak{sp}(\Omega_{I}) \cong \mathfrak{so}(I^{\perp})$, whose elements are traceless. Antisymmetry is ten conditions, leaving the $6$-dimensional space $\{A : \Omega_{I}A \text{ antisymmetric}\}$, on which $A \mapsto A\cdot I$ is injective (an antisymmetric $\beta_{A}$ equal to $-\tfrac12\Omega_{A\cdot I}$ vanishes iff $A\cdot I = 0$, and then $A = 0$ by nondegeneracy), hence a bijection onto $\Lambda^{2}\CS$; $\mathfrak{gl}(\CS)$ is the direct sum of the two parts. The identity lies in the antisymmetric part ($\beta_{1} = \Omega_{I}$) and has trace $4$, so the trace cuts that part to a $5$-dimensional complement of the stabiliser inside $\mathfrak{sl}(\CS)$.

For $U \in I^{\perp}$, $A(U\wedge I)$ is not in the stabiliser, since $R_{U\wedge I}(I) = \ip{U}{I}I - Q(I)U = -Q(I)U \neq 0$, and $U \mapsto A(U\wedge I)$ is linear and injective on $I^{\perp}$. Its image lies in the antisymmetric part by equivariance: under the stabiliser $\mathfrak{so}(I^{\perp})$, $I^{\perp}$ is the $5$-dimensional vector representation and the stabiliser itself is the $10$-dimensional adjoint representation, irreducible and non-isomorphic, while $\mathfrak{gl}(\CS) = \mathfrak{sp}(\Omega_{I}) \oplus \{\text{antisymmetric part}\}$ is a decomposition into $\mathfrak{so}(I^{\perp})$-submodules (both conditions are invariant under conjugation by the stabiliser); the map $U \mapsto A(U\wedge I)$ is $\mathfrak{so}(I^{\perp})$-equivariant, so by Schur's lemma its component in $\mathfrak{sp}(\Omega_{I})$ vanishes. Since the five images are traceless (all of $A(\cdot)$ is), they span the $5$-dimensional traceless antisymmetric part. The real-form statement is Fact \claimref{mass.imported-frozen-point-tractor-connection}'s stabiliser together with the count $15 - 10 = 5$; the action paper's Proposition 5.4 counts nine broken generators for the pair $(I, V)$, of which the five directions of $I^{\perp}$ are the $I$-half. The script confirms the dimensions $10$, $6$ and $5$ by exact rank at $\Lambda = 3$ and checks directly that the five matrices $A(e_{a}\wedge I_{\Lambda})$ are traceless, independent, and have $\Omega A$ antisymmetric.

mass.grip-real.technical:
Let $V_{\R}$ be the real span of $n_{\infty}$, $n_{0}$ and the real slice of the $x$-slot. For $U, V \in V_{\R}$ the generator $A(U\wedge V)$ lies in $\mathfrak{su}(2,2)$, the real form of the reversion form $\Sigma$, the Hermitian form of the conformal spinor space $\CS$, so the moment $M_{U\wedge V}$ is real, and for $I \in V_{\R}$ the grip $P = M(I)$ is a real ambient vector.

For the frozen point $I_{\Lambda}$, $P$ is a real vector of $I_{\Lambda}^{\perp}$, so $m^{2} = Q(P)$ is a value of the real form of signature $(1,4)$ that the frozen point induces on its orthogonal complement.
mass.grip-real.lay: The mass of a composite is defined as the length of a vector, its grip on the cosmological scale. For that to be a physical mass the vector must be real, not complex. This lemma checks that it is: real points give real symmetry generators and real charges, so the grip is real and its length is measured by the de Sitter geometry.

proofs.main:
Conventions: the chart's complex unit is $I_{6}$, the complex unit of the conformal spinor space $\CS$, acting on conformal spinors by right multiplication; numbers formed from conformal spinors (values of the Hermitian form, components, traces) are read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{6}\}$, and the bar is the conjugation that reverses $I_{6}$.

The first conclusion is the chart form of \cite[Prop.~4.5(2)]{ButlerT9} (\claimref{correspondence.reality-conjugation-twistor-form-factor}), which states that the real bivectors act $\Sigma$-anti-Hermitianly; here it is the chart computation, in four steps. The second conclusion is this paper's.

\emph{Step 1, the criterion.} In the block form of Lemma \claimref{mass.chart-form-spin-isomorphism}, $\Sigma = \left(\begin{smallmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{smallmatrix}\right)$, so for $A = \left(\begin{smallmatrix} A_{11} & A_{12} \\ A_{21} & A_{22}\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ the matrix $\Sigma A = \left(\begin{smallmatrix} A_{21} & A_{22} \\ A_{11} & A_{12}\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ is anti-Hermitian iff $A_{12}^{\dagger} = -A_{12}$, $A_{21}^{\dagger} = -A_{21}$ and $A_{22} = -A_{11}^{\dagger}$.

\emph{Step 2, the grading and the translations.} The grading element has $A_{11} = -\tfrac12$, $A_{22} = \tfrac12$, $A_{12} = A_{21} = 0$, and satisfies the criterion. For $x$ in the slice \claimref{note.mass.what-nullity-fixes}, $x = \tfrac{I_{6}}{\sqrt2}K\varepsilon$ with $K$ Hermitian, the translation block of Lemma \claimref{mass.chart-form-spin-isomorphism}(2) is $b_{x} = x\varepsilon = \tfrac{I_{6}}{\sqrt2}K\varepsilon^{2} = -\tfrac{I_{6}}{\sqrt2}K$, anti-Hermitian.

\emph{Step 3, the special conformal generators.} The block of Lemma \claimref{mass.chart-form-spin-isomorphism}(3) is $c_{x} = -x^{\mathsf T}\varepsilon = \tfrac{I_{6}}{\sqrt2}\,\varepsilon K^{\mathsf T}\varepsilon$ (using $\varepsilon^{\mathsf T} = -\varepsilon$), whose adjoint is $-\tfrac{I_{6}}{\sqrt2}\,\varepsilon^{\dagger}\bar{K}\varepsilon^{\dagger} = -\tfrac{I_{6}}{\sqrt2}\,\varepsilon K^{\mathsf T}\varepsilon = -c_{x}$, since $\bar K = K^{\mathsf T}$ and $\varepsilon^{\dagger} = -\varepsilon$: anti-Hermitian.

\emph{Step 4, the Lorentz generators.} For two rotations $R_{U\wedge V}(Z) = \ip{U}{Z}V - \ip{V}{Z}U$, expanding both sides on a vector $Z$ gives
\[
[R_{U\wedge V}, R_{W\wedge Y}] = \ip{U}{W}R_{V\wedge Y} - \ip{U}{Y}R_{V\wedge W} - \ip{V}{W}R_{U\wedge Y} + \ip{V}{Y}R_{U\wedge W}
\]
(the four terms are $R_{U\wedge V}R_{W\wedge Y}Z = \ip{W}{Z}\,R_{U\wedge V}Y - \ip{Y}{Z}\,R_{U\wedge V}W$ minus the same with the pairs exchanged, regrouped by which of $U, V, W, Y$ carries $Z$). For $U = x$, $V = n_{\infty}$, $W = x'$, $Y = n_{0}$ with $x, x'$ in the slice, $\ip{n_{\infty}}{x'} = \ip{x}{n_{0}} = Q(n_{\infty}) = 0$ and $\ip{n_{\infty}}{n_{0}} = 1$ leave $[R_{x\wedge n_{\infty}}, R_{x'\wedge n_{0}}] = \ip{x}{x'}R_{n_{\infty}\wedge n_{0}} + R_{x\wedge x'}$. Hence $A(x\wedge x') = [A(x\wedge n_{\infty}), A(x'\wedge n_{0})] - \ip{x}{x'}A(n_{\infty}\wedge n_{0})$ lies in $\mathfrak{su}(2,2)$, a Lie algebra, because $\ip{x}{x'}$ is real.

\emph{The span, and the grip.} The pairs $n_{\infty}\wedge n_{0}$ (one), $x\wedge n_{\infty}$ (four), $x\wedge n_{0}$ (four) and $x\wedge x'$ (six) span $\Lambda^{2}V_{\R}$, of dimension $15$, so every $A(U\wedge V)$ with $U, V \in V_{\R}$ is in $\mathfrak{su}(2,2)$, and $M_{A}$ is real there because $\Sigma A$ anti-Hermitian makes $\bar{Z}\cdot AZ$ imaginary. Then $\ip{P}{U} = M_{U\wedge I}$ is real for every $U \in V_{\R}$, and since the pairing restricted to $V_{\R}$ is a real nondegenerate form (the form of signature $(2,4)$ of Fact \claimref{mass.imported-flat-model-twistor-chart-infinity}; in the basis $n_{\infty}, n_{0}$ and the slice \claimref{note.mass.what-nullity-fixes} its Gram matrix is $\left(\begin{smallmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{smallmatrix}\right) \oplus \operatorname{diag}(1,-1,-1,-1)$), $P \in V_{\R}$. The last clause is $P \perp I_{\Lambda}$ with Fact \claimref{mass.imported-frozen-point-tractor-connection}. The script checks the commutator identity on the real points, the anti-Hermiticity of the generators for real pairs on four real points, and the reality of the pairings of $P$ with a real basis of $V_{\R}$.
